description.narrative: The Project aims to improve rural livelihoods and reduce rural poverty through improved irrigation service delivery, enhanced agricultural practices, and strengthened water resources management to increase the productivity of irrigated agriculture in Chhattisgarh.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: 1. Attain more effective management, development, and operation and maintenance (O&M) of irrigation systems by Water Resource Department (WRD) and water users associations (WUAs) for improved irrigation service delivery. 2. Improve agricultural practices for increased yields and expand area of rabi (dry season) and more diversified cropping.

1. Improved quality of O&M in irrigation systems (downstream users with reliable water supply in Kharif season -2 years post rehabilitation and upgrading (R&U) Progress/Status: Designs for 167 schemes (200,000 ha) were completed. Contracts for 148 schemes (four schemes dropped subsequently) for R&U works have been awarded out of which 144 schemes are reported completed, covering an area of about 173984ha . Data Source: 1. Project implementation progress reports 2. Irrigation system performance, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) for resources and quality of O&M works 3 Agricultural productivity M&E under the Project and by Department of Agriculture (DOA) 4. Quality of design and construction works by third-party inspection 5. Project implementation progress reports 6. Annual reporting by state agencies Baseline value: N

2. Better performance of new irrigation systems at least 90% kharif (wet season) and 40% rabi cropping intensity - 2 years post R & U Progress/Status: In 50 CIDP systems covering 101,312 ha, 2012 Kharif cropping intensity maintained at 100%. Rabi 2012-13 average cropping intensity of about 52% (52,836 ha.) has been achieved. Baseline value: N

3. Higher yields (at least 3.3. tons rice) and cropping intensity (130%) in irrigation systems - 3 years post R&U Progress/Status: In 2012 Kharif higher yields achieved (5.9t/ha in 50 irrigation systems covering about 101,312ha. under Intensive Intervention Program in 2012). Rabi area gradually expanded and in Rabi 2012-13, about 52% of the command area has been covered for cultivation. Baseline value: N

4. More diversified and rabi crops produced (40% rabi intensity and decrease in rice growth in kharif-3 years post R&U) Progress/Status: Crop diversification program, which was expected after R&U, has commenced ahead of schedule in 2007. However, during initial years, Rabi cropping intensity was low because irrigated area was restricted due to R&U works. Now, mainly due to “water saving” through maximizing the use of rainfall during Kharif, due to project interventions Rabi Cropping Intensity expanded to reach about 52% during 2012-13. Rabi diversification extended/ introduced to all the schemes under IIP. Also, cash crops (like groundnut, mustard, sunflower, gram, maize etc.) have been introduced. Areas under Intensive Intervention Program (IIP), Community Organizers facilitating WUA-managed: a) irrigation distribution (within WUA command areas), b) WUA-managed seed supply, c) supply of other inputs through WUAs, and d) WUA-managed marketing (Partnerships with Private Sector) which is continued during 2012 kharif and 2012-13 Rabi season also. In Rabi 2012-13 rice productions is strictly discouraged and more emphasis is being given for cultivating wheat, mustard, lentil, gram and sunflower. Non paddy crop cultivation has been taken up in all schemes under IIP. Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.
4. Improved capacity and willingness of farmers to engage in rabi cropping and diversified farming in irrigation system.

Output: 1. Institutional strengthening and capacity development for WRD. Indicator: 1 WRD with improved functions for units for participatory irrigation management (PIM), social development, design, and dam safety by Year 3 Progress/Status: PIM unit functioning with one executive engineer and nine assistant engineers and one PIM Expert at Raipur, Ambikapur and Bilaspur training centres in addition to office staff. SDU was not functional and during the Mission (6-9 Aug 2012), SDU was revived with the assignment of one Executive Engineer and two assistant engineers. WRD initiated process for approval of PSC for engaging experts for SDU. Experts could not be engaged till loan closure on 31 March 2013. Data Source: 1. Review missions 2. Progress reports 3. Irrigation system performance M&E for resources and quality of O&M works 4. Agricultural productivity M&E under Project and by DA 5. Specialized studies 6. M&E systems established in WUAs 7. Revenue records and state budget 8. Surveys of stakeholders Target year: 2009 Target value: Y

Output: 1. Institutional strengthening and capacity development for WRD. Indicator: 2. Capacity building ongoing for WRD and improved management information system, information technology and other resources for effective management by year 2 Progress/Status: WRD's needs assessment and capacity development programs have been prepared and about 2064 WRD staff have been trained in PIM, water management aspects, ADB procedures etc. A participatory workshop on the capacity building plan was organized with WRD staff. Training manuals for trainers and trainees were developed and training provided to WRD staff. In addition, WRD staff participated in TA-managed WUA capacity building (PIM Training conducted for WUAs by NGO; and intensive interventions). To strengthen PIM Unit, PIM expert has joined office with effect from 1 February 2012. The training center buildings of Ambikapur, Raipur and Bilaspur have been completed. A training center development strategy was prepared by the PMU but need to be revised as it is not ensuring a long term institutionalization. ADB engaged capacity development expert to develope strategy for short and long term capacity development for WRD officers. Report has been submitted by the expert. Target year: 2008 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved institutional framework and capacity development for WUAs Indicator: 3. New framework for PIM with greater WUA authority and WRD accountability by year 2 Progress/Status: Progressive PIM act approved in 2006.
The second amendment to the PIM Act includes change/addition in the rule numbers 37 and 83 and section 5, 8 and 11 of the PIM act, which was sent for approval of GOC and notification in Gazette. Amendment to rule number 37 has been notified in the gazette on 23 December 2011 and amendment to Rule 83 is added and published in gazette notification on 3.8.2012. Cabinet approval to the proposal sent by WRD on 23 September 2011 for amendment to section 5, 8 and 11 of the PIM act section is still awaited. On 10 August 2010, based on the approval received from the Department of Finance (DOF), WRD approved the proposal to enhance the percentage of water fee to be shared with WUAs from 25% to 50% to be implemented only for CIDP schemes which was later extended to the entire state through a second note from WRD dated 29 September 2010. After the approval of WRD and concurrence of the Law Department, a note to modify the relevant rules to increase the share of WUAs from 25% to 50% has been sent to GOC for cabinet approval on 4 May 2011 which is still awaited.
3rd amendment to allow WUAs to retain part of the collected water fee at the source has been submitted for approval of the Government of Chattisgarh on 29 June 2011- Government approval still awaited Target year: 2008 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved institutional framework and capacity development for WUAs Indicator: 4. Capacity development program for WUAs established and WUAs enrolled by year 2. Progress/Status: WUA capacity building has been carried out at three levels: (i) Experiential capacity building through WUA-managed interventions under Intensive Intervention Program (IIP). In Rabi 2012-13, 50 CIDP systems (covering about 100,000ha), WUA capacity development continued through WUA-managed Irrigation O&M and agriculture interventions. WUAs are involved in input-output marketing and are developed as “Multi-functional organizations” (ii) Periodic capacity building through formal sessions in the balance CIDP systems and (iii) State-wide basic (formal) training on PIM for selected WUA Representatives from all the 1324 WUAs in the State and sharing IIP strategy, process and experience gained in CIDP pilot schemes with Non-CIDP WUAs. Target year: 2008 Target value: Y

Output: 2. Improved institutional framework and capacity development for WUAs Indicator: 5. Higher resources flowing to WUAs (and WRD) for irrigation O&M by year 3 Progress/Status: WRD/PMU released payments to 369 WUAs ( CIDP-86 and non-CIDP-273)as grant out of the 902 eligible WUAs (CIDP-189 and non-CIDP-713) for which list was finalised by NGO. Return of a share of the water fee by DOF/WRD to WUA as per PIM Act provision is still to be implemented. Target year: 2009 Target value: Y

Output: 3. R&U of existing irrigation schemes leading to improved performance Indicator: 6. R&U of minor and medium schemes covering over 177,130 ha with increased cropping intensity by end of Project. Progress/Status: R&U works of 144 minor and medium schemes covering about 173984ha are reported to be completed.
